findings.finding: April4 meeting context reports Croune producing Towneley letter datedMarch25,1667; description and observations requested. Footnote says letter not entered in Letter-Book and points to printed issue25p457. Later editor negative inventory, not authenticated archival loss.

July11 reports Croune received Gascoigne instrument from Towneley; July25 records Hooke bringing Towneley instrument and a different own design. Operator ordered to make same kind for repository. Claim of5000/possible40000partsperinch for diagonal design is nominal, not accuracy.

Request for renewed consideration followed by October10 context: Croune produces instrument, Society judges ingenious/useful, requests retention and another example made by same unnamed artist; Hooke also produces cheaper design and is ordered to make one and describe use. Commissioning is not completed manufacture or calibrated trial.

October31 context reports Hooke producing own designs, including astronomical instrument considered easier/cheaper than Towneley; requested written account and communication to Towneley. Not proof of comparative accuracy.
November7 heading precedes report that scheme/description ready in secretary hands; next heading literallyNovember4. Out-of-order label retained, not silently corrected.

Under literalNovember4 heading, Hooke description read/ordered registered; footnote refers RegisterIIIp227 and printissue29p541.
